newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: COCONUT OIL - Philippine prices seen softer.
newsitem.headline: COCONUT OIL - Philippine prices seen softer.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to trade sideways to down, dampened by news of good soybean crop in the United States, traders said on Monday.
"I expect the market to open tentative to softer for the week due to the USDA soybean report and improving copra production in the local front," one trader told Reuters.
Copra supply in the southern Mindanao island has improved, an official of the government-agency Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) said.
But traders said they do not expect any dramatic rise in supply in the next few days.
Reports of a copra supply crunch in Mindanao following a delayed harvest due to persistent rains sent prices soaring in the past weeks.
"Copra harvest in Mindanao is our salvation. Luzon (harvest) is a goner," said one dealer.
Coconut growing areas ravaged by typhoons in Luzon island last year were still recovering from the damage.

Philippine coconut millers are now selling directly their products to buyers with slight improvements in copra supply from Mindanao and some parts of the Bicol region in north Luzon island, traders said.
But "origin sellers were reluctant to commit physical volume," said one trader.
Nevertheless, "trade on paper," is gaining ground, the trader said.
"I expect coconut oil export to reach 75,000 tonnes this month," said one trader.

Philippine coconut oil exports dropped to an average 66,823 tonnes monthly from January to September this year compared to 113,940 tonnes monthly last year, the trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines (UCAP) said.
"I expect coconut oil prices to drop up to $725 from $740 per tonne CIF for nearby months in Europe, and below the current price of 33.75 cents per lb CIF in the United States," said one trader.
UCAP said the Philippines exported 48,000 tonnes of coconut oil from October 1 to 10 and, 12,000 tonnes of copra meal.
